risks.title: SSN encryption key exposed in source code
risks.description: The AES-256 key for encrypting/decrypting Social Security Numbers is a plaintext constant in PKG_SECURITY.pkb. Anyone with source code access can decrypt all stored SSNs.
risks.impact: Full exposure of all employee PII (SSNs); GDPR/HIPAA/state data privacy law violations; regulatory penalties.
risks.likelihood: HIGH — any developer or DBA with repo access
risks.migration_impact: During modernization the key must be rotated; all encrypted SSN values must be re-encrypted with a new key managed through a proper key management service. This is a blocking pre-migration security task.

risks.title: Authentication is effectively unenforced
risks.description: PKG_SECURITY.authenticate is a stub: password comparison against stored credentials is not implemented (TODO comment). Combined with no brute-force protection, the system has no actual authentication barrier.
risks.impact: Any user knowing a valid username can log in without the correct password.
risks.likelihood: HIGH — in current state this affects all users
risks.migration_impact: Authentication must be rebuilt from scratch in any modernized system. User credentials must be migrated to a proper identity provider.

risks.title: SQL injection in employee search
risks.description: PKG_EMPLOYEE.search_employees is vulnerable to SQL injection via the p_filter_clause parameter. A malicious user could exfiltrate the entire database, modify data, or execute OS commands via UTL_FILE.
risks.impact: Full database compromise; data exfiltration; ransomware injection point.
risks.likelihood: MEDIUM — requires authenticated access to HRMS
risks.migration_impact: Any REST API or service that wraps this procedure inherits the vulnerability. Must be fixed before or during migration.

risks.title: Payroll run data corruption on failure
risks.description: calculate_payroll commits every 50 employees. A failure mid-run leaves a partially calculated payroll run with no rollback path. Employees may receive incorrect pay or no pay.
risks.impact: Payroll errors leading to under/overpayment; compliance violations; employee relations impact.
risks.likelihood: MEDIUM — any DB error or timeout mid-run triggers this
risks.migration_impact: The partial-commit pattern must not be replicated in any modernized payroll service. The new system needs transactional payroll calculation.

risks.title: Annual tax/compliance value rot
risks.description: Federal tax brackets (2024), FICA wage base ($168,600), and state tax rates are hard-coded. They will silently calculate incorrectly for any tax year after 2024 unless a developer manually updates and redeploys the package.
risks.impact: Incorrect payroll tax withholding; IRS/state penalties; potential class-action liability.
risks.likelihood: HIGH — guaranteed to occur each new tax year
risks.migration_impact: Migration must treat these as configuration, not code. Design a TAX_CONFIG table with effective dates.

risks.title: Circular dependency blocks independent deployment
risks.description: PKG_EMPLOYEE and PKG_PAYROLL have a compile-time circular dependency. Neither can be independently deployed, tested, or modernized. Any change to one risks breaking the other.
risks.impact: Tight coupling blocks modular migration; any refactor to either package requires coordinated change to both.
risks.migration_impact: Must be broken before independent microservice extraction. A shared domain event or orchestration layer pattern is needed.

risks.title: DBMS_SCHEDULER jobs not in source control
risks.description: The scheduled jobs for PKG_NOTIFICATION.process_queue and PKG_LEAVE.run_monthly_accrual are inferred from code comments but their DDL was not found in the repository. They exist only in the live database.
risks.impact: Scheduler jobs lost on environment rebuild; silent failure of notifications and leave accruals.
risks.likelihood: HIGH — any environment refresh from source would lose these jobs
risks.migration_impact: Before migration, DBA must extract scheduler job DDL and add to version control.
risks.evidence: COMP-SCHEDULER-JOBS — inferred from PKG_NOTIFICATION.pkb and PKG_LEAVE.pkb comments

risks.title: Oracle Forms Java applet — browser support end-of-life
risks.description: Oracle Forms 12c serves its client via a Java applet or Java Web Start. Major browsers dropped Java plugin support (Chrome 2015, Firefox 2017). Users require a specific JRE version and potentially Internet Explorer or a dedicated terminal.
risks.impact: Expanding set of users unable to access HRMS; increasing support burden for legacy browser/JRE combinations.
risks.likelihood: HIGH — already an issue for most modern browsers
risks.migration_impact: The Oracle Forms layer is a primary modernization driver. Any web-based replacement eliminates this risk.

risks.title: Unimplemented integration stubs
risks.description: Time & Attendance import (import_time_attendance) and LDAP/AD org sync (sync_org_structure) are stubs. Any process relying on them receives no data and no error.
risks.impact: Time & attendance data not imported; org structure not synchronized with directory.
risks.likelihood: HIGH — stubs are permanently non-functional unless developed
risks.migration_impact: Any migration plan that depends on these integrations being functional must implement them first.

risks.title: Leave balance view shows incorrect available days
risks.description: VW_LEAVE_SUMMARY omits PENDING_DAYS from the AVAILABLE calculation. Employees viewing their balance via the view see more available leave than they actually have, potentially leading to double-booking.
risks.impact: Over-allocation of leave; HR/manager confusion; payroll impact for unpaid leave.
risks.likelihood: MEDIUM — affects anyone using the VW_LEAVE_SUMMARY view
risks.migration_impact: The correct formula must be used in any replacement system. Migration data validation must check for existing over-allocated leave.

risks.title: Vendor lock-in: ADP benefits feed is hardcoded format
risks.description: PKG_INTEGRATION.export_benefits_feed generates a fixed-width file in a format specific to ADP. Changing benefits vendors requires code changes to PKG_INTEGRATION.
risks.impact: Inability to switch benefits vendors without code changes; ADP dependency baked into core payroll package.
risks.likelihood: LOW — only triggered by vendor change
risks.migration_impact: Modernized integration layer should abstract format from vendor; use a configurable export format.

risks.title: Missing COBRA/access revocation/final pay in termination flow
risks.description: PKG_EMPLOYEE.terminate_employee has TODO comments for COBRA notification, system access revocation, and final pay calculation. These are compliance-critical steps missing from the implemented flow.
risks.impact: COBRA compliance failure; security risk from unrevoked access; incorrect final paychecks.
risks.likelihood: HIGH — every termination goes through this incomplete flow
risks.migration_impact: These features must be implemented before or during migration.

risks.title: Employee number race condition
risks.description: generate_emp_number uses SELECT MAX+1 without locking. Concurrent employee creation can generate duplicate numbers.
risks.impact: Unique constraint violation on concurrent hire; one transaction fails; HR must retry.
risks.migration_impact: Replace with sequence-based ID generation in new system (already available as SEQ_EMPLOYEE).
